narrative: The model estimated that you have a 34% chance of bad credit—roughly one in three. That does not mean default is certain, but it is above the risk level the lender accepts, so your application was denied. The most influential factor was the amount you requested. At 2,528 DM, it was below the average approved request of about 3,020 DM, and it counted in your favour by lowering the assessed risk. The second most important factor was the business purpose of the loan. Business loans are only a small share of approved applications, yet this detail also worked in your favour in the assessment. Third was your one year at your current residence, which is shorter than the approved average of about three years; even so, it too counted toward good credit. Because your three leading factors were favourable, the denial came from the combined effect of other, less influential details rather than from these main points. Next, ask the lender for a written explanation of the decision, check your credit report for errors, and discuss whether a different loan amount or structure, a guarantor, or waiting until your account and employment records are stronger could improve a future application.
